questions.prompt:

The train leaves at 06 48.
The journey takes 12 hours and 35 minutes.

Find the time when Tara arrives.

61    63    64    66    68    69

The table shows the probability of how a student, chosen at random, travels to school.

|  | Bus | Walk | Car | Other |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.4 | 0.32 | 0.17 |  |

Complete the table. [Enter the missing probability for "Other".]

|  | Bus | Walk | Car | Other |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.4 | 0.32 | 0.17 |  |

Find the expected number of students that walk to school.

**Without using a calculator**, work out 1 5/6 ÷ 11/15.

You must show all your working and give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
questions.criteria: 1 mark: converts the mixed number to an improper fraction (1 5/6 = 11/6). 1 mark: multiplies by the reciprocal with working shown (11/6 × 15/11 = 15/6 or equivalent). 1 mark: final answer 2 1/2 given as a mixed number in simplest form. Working must be shown for full marks.

questions.prompt: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 48 and 80.

P = 2wy²/3

Find the positive value of y when P = 108 and w = 8.

AB is the column vector (7, −3).

Find 3AB. [Give your answer as a vector, e.g. "(a, b)".]

AB is the column vector (7, −3).

Find |AB|, the magnitude of AB.

A bronze sphere has radius 3.6 cm.
The density of bronze is 8.05 g/cm³.

Find the mass of the sphere.
Give your answer **in kilograms**, correct to the nearest gram.

[The volume, V, of a sphere with radius r is V = (4/3)πr³.]

[Density = mass ÷ volume.]

Oliver sent 22% more messages in June than in May.
He sent 305 messages in June.

Find how many more messages he sent in June than in May.

The graph of y = 2x + 1 is drawn on the grid.

By shading the **unwanted** regions of the grid, find and label the region R which satisfies these inequalities.

y ≥ 2x + 1        y ≥ 1        4x + 3y < 12

[This is a drawing task. If you cannot shade the grid, describe in words where region R lies — give its boundary lines and the coordinates of its corner points.]
questions.criteria: 1 mark per boundary handled correctly: region satisfies y ≥ 2x + 1 (on or above/left of the drawn line), y ≥ 1 (on or above the horizontal line y = 1), and 4x + 3y < 12 (below the line through (3, 0) and (0, 4)). 1 mark: region R correctly identified/labelled — the triangular region with vertices (0, 1), (2.25, 1) and (0.9, 2.8). A clear verbal description naming the three boundaries and the triangular region earns full credit.

Find the coordinates of the point where the line 4x + y = 9 intersects the curve y + x² = 5.

You must show all your working.
questions.criteria: 1 mark: substitutes y = 9 − 4x into y + x² = 5 (or eliminates y equivalently). 1 mark: derives x² − 4x + 4 = 0. 1 mark: solves the quadratic, e.g. factorises to (x − 2)² = 0. 1 mark: x = 2. 1 mark: y = 1, final answer (2, 1). Working must be shown; answer only earns at most 1 mark.
